main_body: A pew drawn in side profile: a tall backrest post on the left (x6-10) and a seat section on the right with three red cushion panels stacked vertically, separated by tan bands, and a base at the bottom.
top_band: At the middle of the seat body (x~14) the column starts with a dark outline at row 13, then a thin tan/orange band of about 2 rows (rows 14-15), and then the red cushion face starts at row 16. There is no real top surface.
evidence: The pew is drawn as a flat vertical elevation. The tall backrest is a plain vertical strip, and the seat is three red panels stacked vertically that read as vertical faces, not as a seat seen from above. The only horizontal surface is a 2px tan band at the top, which is a rim. The tan bands between the red panels are thin dividers. There is no seat surface visible from above, so it fails the 3/4 contract as a side elevation, like the side elevation chair in the guide.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown beside the wood, which is acceptable. The wood strip has about 3 tones (tan, mid brown, dark brown) and the red cushions are big flat fills of about 3 tones, with no grain, dots or stitching. The red panels are 5x5 or larger areas of a single colour. Next to the stall and well references, which carry many colours per tile, the tiles are mostly 2-4 colours, so it is much thinner and flatter.
